misconceptions: Any contrary opinion counts as proof.

semantic_axes.description: To refute a claim is to establish that it is false; to rebut it is to answer with a contrary argument, which may not conclusively disprove it.

edges.boundary_rule: To refute a claim is to establish that it is false; to rebut it is to answer with a contrary argument, which may not conclusively disprove it.

misconceptions.M2: Assuming a rebuttal is always conclusive.
misconceptions.M3: Mistaking an emphatic tone for evidence.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Fatima's response to a criticism?

beats.text: Fatima tells classmates she thinks the criticism of the play is unfair and offers a different interpretation.
beats.reason: She challenges the view without disproving it.

beats.text: She speaks confidently, but neither side produces proof settling the disagreement.
beats.decisive_clue: confidence does not prove claim wrong
beats.reason: A confident delivery does not supply the evidence needed to settle the issue.

chains.feedback_short: A confident delivery does not supply the evidence needed to settle the issue.
chains.feedback_deep: Refute means show a claim is false through sufficient evidence or reasoning. Rebut means respond to a claim with an opposing argument, even if the disagreement remains unresolved. A confident delivery does not supply the evidence needed to settle the issue.
chains.contrast_rule: Rebut argues back; refute proves wrong.

hints.contrast: Rebut argues back; refute proves wrong.
